entry.title: Oväntade effekten på kronan: ”Vi ser det helt motsatta”
entry.summary:

entry.title: Hans led av svår pollenallergi – medicin gav lindring
entry.summary: Göteborgaren Hans Zetterberg fick svår gräspollenallergi när han var 16 år gammal. Något som påverkat honom starkt större delen av livet. ”Ögonen sved och tårades så att de till slut inte gick att öppna”, säger han. Men för fem år sedan fick han en medicin, som fungerar som ett vaccin, och som gjort livet betydligt lättare.”Jag vill leva mitt liv som jag vill”, säger Hans.

entry.title: Slow image loading
entry.summary: Mar 30, 18:36 UTC Identified - While we are managing to serve some of the image traffic, clearly we aren't keeping up with demand and loading times are still very slow. We have however identified the bottleneck and will be working to address it. Mar 30, 17:00 UTC Update - Since things have been fine for now, we will keep monitoring but consider the issue presumably fixed. Mar 29, 00:19 UTC Monitoring - A fix has been implemented, but we will need to wait for a similar failure as the last times to see it perform live before we judge it as sufficient. Mar 17, 20:01 UTC Investigating - Image loading is extremely slow again in some region. While we have a rough idea of what is the cause, it is not so easy to address. We're actively working on it.

entry.title: Jumboplats på pressfrihetslistan: ”Vanligast är anklagelser om att stötta terror”
entry.summary:
• Turkiet bekräftar gripandet av den svenske journalisten Joakim Medin och meddelar att han misstänks för terrorkoppling, rapporterar nyhetsbyrån AFP. Han anklagas formellt för delaktighet i den terrorstämplade kurdiska organisationen PKK och för att ha förolämpat Turkiets president Erdogan.

  • Angående pressfrihet så ligger Turkiet ligger långt nere i Reportrar utan gränsers mätning om pressfriheten i världen, nämligen på plats 158 av 180 länder, säger Katja Magnusson, utrikesreporter på Ekot och tidigare korrespondent i Turkiet.

  • ”En av de vanligaste anklagelserna handlar om att stötta terrororganisationer, eller på olika sätt ha kopplingar till eller samröre med terrororganisationer”, säger Katja Magnusson.

entry.title: Watch wind whirl from the Sun
entry.summary:
Video: 00:00:43
Aside from sunlight, the Sun sends out a gusty stream of particles called the solar wind. The ESA-led Solar Orbiter mission is the first to capture on camera this wind flying out from the Sun in a twisting, whirling motion. The solar wind particles spiral outwards as if caught in a cyclone that extends millions of kilometres from the Sun. Solar wind rains down on Earth's atmosphere constantly, but the intensity of this rain depends on solar activity. More than just a space phenomenon, solar wind can disrupt our telecommunication and navigation systems. Solar Orbiter is on a mission to uncover the origin of the solar wind. entry.title: Euclid opens data treasure trove, offers glimpse of deep fields
entry.summary: On 19 March 2025, the European Space Agency’s Euclid mission released its first batch of survey data, including a preview of its deep fields. Here, hundreds of thousands of galaxies in different shapes and sizes take centre stage and show a glimpse of their large-scale organisation in the cosmic web.

entry.title: Euclid is back – 26 million galaxies and counting
entry.summary:
Video: 00:06:44
The European Space Agency’s Euclid mission has scouted out the three areas in the sky where it will eventually provide the deepest observations of its mission. In just one week of observations, with one scan of each region so far, Euclid already spotted 26 million galaxies. The farthest of those are up to 10.5 billion light-years away. In the coming years, Euclid will pass over these three regions tens of times, capturing many more faraway galaxies, making these fields truly ‘deep’ by the end of the nominal mission in 2030. The first glimpse of 63 square degrees of the sky, the equivalent area of more than 300 times the full Moon, already gives an impressive preview of the scale of Euclid’s grand cosmic atlas when the mission is complete. This atlas will cover one-third of the entire sky – 14 000 square degrees – in this high-quality detail.
